A horizontal scale of the IUCN Red List categories as a row of coloured boxes from left to right, getting darker towards extinction: Least Concern (green), Near Threatened (light green), Vulnerable (yellow), Endangered (orange), Critically Endangered (red), Extinct in the Wild (dark purple), Extinct (black). A bracket over Vulnerable, Endangered and Critically Endangered. Small simple animal icons under some boxes: a Cross River gorilla under Critically Endangered and a drill under Endangered. Separate grey boxes at the side for Data Deficient and Not Evaluated.

An outline map of Nigeria with state boundaries shown faintly. Green shaded areas or markers show the locations of the national parks: Kainji Lake (west, on the River Niger in Niger and Kwara States, with the lake drawn in blue), Old Oyo (south-west, in Oyo State), Okomu (south, in Edo State), Cross River (south-east, in Cross River State, with two sections), Gashaka-Gumti (east, in Taraba and Adamawa States on the Cameroon border), Chad Basin (north-east, in Borno and Yobe States, several small sections), Kamuku (north-central, in Kaduna State), and Yankari Game Reserve (north-east, in Bauchi State) shown with a different symbol (an orange marker). Rivers Niger and Benue and Lake Chad drawn in blue.
